no deadline reset Bare trace Exact existing acknowledgement, routing and final output Both channels, hash widths and scopes Frozen destination text and correct reply context 55/60-second boundaries and rollover Existing report reserve, expiry and busy release remain intact

For identity-sensitive tests, decrypt the actual outgoing discovery request with the selected full target's shared secret and verify the RTC replay tag. Include another identity with a different remaining key suffix so a name-only or partial key implementation cannot pass. Unknown/ambiguous tests should observe packet types/counts and pool ownership, not merely the returned label.

For immutability, force a queue rejection or allocation retry, then rename or evict the cache entry before transmission. Inspect emitted text and the actual discovery identity. Retain the existing real Dispatcher tests; do not rely only on the legacy immediate-acknowledgement seam.

docs.title: Validation gates
docs.text:
1. Run focused storage, acknowledgement, targeted trace and network tests.
  2. Run pio test -e native -e native_sensor -e native_kiss_modem.
  3. Run the sensor AddressSanitizer suite using the existing working host configuration; record its leak-check setting/runtime setup.
  4. Build Xiao_nrf52_bme680_sensor, Xiao_nrf52_sensor_baseline, Xiao_nrf52_companion_radio_usb, Xiao_nrf52_repeater, and Xiao_nrf52_room_server; generate applicable DFU and UF2 artifacts.
  5. Run bin/check-sensor-boundaries.sh, whitespace checks and strict MkDocs.
  6. Compare static RAM/flash with the pre-change build. Keep bounded stack/static storage and avoid a per-request heap allocation or new persistence writes.
  7. Record exact results, revision/working-tree status and artifact checksums. Produce a uniquely named sensor OTA if packaging is requested; do not flash or publish automatically.

Physical acceptance, when hardware is available: advertise a known named repeater, request it by prefix, verify the exact named acknowledgement and usual trace result, then repeat after a rename and with an unusable name. Confirm a pending request retains its original label while a later accepted request uses the updated name. Check unknown/ambiguous errors, both channels and the unchanged 60-second ceiling. Mark physical evidence pending until actually performed.

docs.title: Completion criteria
docs.text:
Every accepted targeted trace names the same full identity used for discovery, using a frozen full-name label or the defined prefix fallback. All rejection paths and bare trace behaviour remain unchanged. Messages remain single-part, UTF-8 safe and bounded. Ownership, retry, scope and timing regressions pass, with hardware results explicitly distinguished from software tests.

This change concerns acknowledgement text. It does not resolve or diagnose the existing sensor-versus-Zen discovery failure.

docs.title: Trace discovery repair and stationary-sensor advert fallback
docs.text:
Status: software implemented and tested; physical acceptance pending. See the implementation validation. Date: 2026-10-25. Sensor baseline: 5add24af; Zen comparison: 6ba09b28.

This plan implements the findings in the sensor/Zen discovery review, together with login-free advert-route fallback. The sensor is stationary, so retaining observed routes is useful. Repeaters and radio conditions can still change; every candidate must be tested by a new TRACE before reporting a result.

docs.title: 1. Required user-visible behaviour
docs.text:
Keep the existing commands and output:

!hillvue trace 7188
Trace requested to Hilltop Repeater, please wait up to 60 seconds.

Preserve full-key prefix resolution, frozen destination name or lowercase prefix fallback, unknown/ambiguous errors, bare trace acknowledgement, final sensor-to- target node ordering, averaged bidirectional SNR and usual result formatting.

For targeted traces, obtain a route through authenticated discovery where possible. Establish first contact when needed and publicly permitted. If no authenticated route is obtained, try a stored route inferred from that target's verified flooded adverts. A usable advert route must allow tracing without any successful login. Never require an administrator password for tracing.

Use one immutable deadline from command acceptance: stop discovery/probing on the first running poll at 55 seconds, reserve the final five seconds for report delivery, and release trace ownership by the first running poll at 60 seconds. No login, cache hit, retry, late response or new advert extends these deadlines. Already transmitting packets stay Dispatcher-owned until completion/recovery. RF receipt and application scheduling cannot be guaranteed by the deadline.

The normal final trace text stays unchanged. Status/debug evidence identifies whether the candidate came from authenticated discovery or an advert hint. Neither a login response nor a cached route is itself a successful trace result.

docs.title: 2. Concrete routing and first-contact policy
docs.text:
Recommended default sequence after acknowledgement:

  1. Send one ordinary authenticated path-discovery request. Existing clients get the fast path and avoid an unnecessary login.
  2. On no usable response, if public guest login is enabled, send exactly one anonymous login using the empty public guest credential. It includes the sensor's full public key, allowing an unknown requester to establish contact.
  3. After an authenticated protocol-valid login response, issue the second and final discovery request with a fresh durable timestamp. Do not substitute the login response's route for freshly matched discovery in this first repair.
  4. If an authenticated route is found, probe it first. Its second probe may use another current authenticated route or a compatible advert alternative.
  5. If authentication/discovery cannot produce a route, select an advert hint and probe it. Use a second distinct advert candidate when available; otherwise a bounded retry of the same route is allowed while time remains.
  6. If no candidate exists, remain passively eligible for a new verified advert during the owned request, until insufficient work time remains for a probe. No additional discovery flood or background scan is generated. End with the appropriate bounded failure.

A configured off policy skips guest login. Following the first unanswered request it can make one remaining ordinary discovery attempt if that can fit; otherwise transition directly to fallback. It must not use all remaining time waiting on authentication while an eligible fallback is available. A login that is not acknowledged transitions to fallback rather than another identical unauthenticated first-contact cycle.

Default public mode sends one empty credential, never a password list. Do not reuse the sensor's incoming management passwords or Zen's saved credentials. Protected guest passwords are outside the initial implementation: tracing such a target can use adverts, or an already established client entry. Add sensor-only admin/local configuration get trace.login and set trace.login public|off, with a small versioned policy record separate from upstream NodePrefs. A failed policy save must report failure and retain the previous effective setting.

The target determines the role granted by its login policy. An empty credential could unexpectedly match a misconfigured empty admin password. Do not claim the wire protocol guarantees a guest role: reject an unexpected admin grant for the first-contact workflow, record it, and use advert fallback. Never perform admin commands, copy credentials, or attempt to undo the target's ACL automatically. A login necessarily changes remote client state if accepted; local management ACLs and saved management routes must remain untouched.

docs.title: 3. Time allocation and traffic bounds
docs.text:
Keep the current acknowledgement admission/watchdog policy, constrained by the overall deadline. Add an absolute control cutoff at 25 seconds from acceptance so primary discovery/login cannot consume the whole work window. It includes any time already spent acknowledging; it is not another 25-second timer after acknowledgement.

Control stage Maximum stage lifetime, including queue/TX/reply wait Initial authenticated discovery 6 seconds One public guest login 8 seconds Final authenticated discovery 6 seconds

Each stage deadline is the earlier of its entry time plus this limit and the 25-second control cutoff. Reply wait begins at actual TX start but cannot extend that stage deadline. Queue/CAD/duty delays consume the same allowance. A quick valid response immediately advances the workflow. If the estimated transmission cannot fit, skip it and use fallback. On slow profiles these stages can end before a valid but slow response; the fixed user-requested cap takes precedence. No timer callback queries the transmitting radio.

At the control cutoff, cancel owned queued control packets and select an available route. Do not free an in-flight packet. Do not queue probes that cannot fit their estimate and the remaining work time. If an unusually slow in-flight acknowledgement/control packet occupies the radio past this point, wait only within the existing work deadline; no phase is entitled to a fresh allowance.

Probe windows retain airtime awareness, divide remaining work among the remaining allowed probe attempts, and share the 55-second cutoff with retry pause/settling/grace. The two-probe total is global: authenticated-route and advert-route probing do not each get two attempts. If the first authenticated route fails, prefer a distinct fresh/previously validated compatible advert route for the remaining attempt when no better authenticated alternative exists.

Maximum potentially emitting sensor packets per targeted operation:

  • One public acknowledgement.
  • Two ordinary discovery requests total.
  • One anonymous public guest login.
  • Two TRACE probes total across all route sources.
  • At most two final public report parts.

Thus at most eight application-originated emitting packets, excluding unrelated commands and other nodes' forwarding. Only definitely-unsent local rejections may retry within a stage lease. Never repeat an uncertain emission beyond that stage's count. Late replies do not create extra login/discovery/probe submissions.

docs.title: 4. Correct login protocol and transaction ownership
docs.text:
Add a separate bounded TraceGuestLogin owner and a TraceFirstContact controller. Reuse the existing discovery/probe owners rather than making login look like an ordinary telemetry response. Keep the selected full target key, control context, current generation and retired-response ownership independent of the mutable name cache.

Stock 1.18 login replies begin with the target's RTC timestamp followed by RESP_SERVER_LOGIN_OK and role/version fields. They do not echo the request's discovery tag. Validate decrypted packet ownership, full target identity, expected response shape/code, current login state, actual login TX start, profile and remaining time. Account for encryption padding. Explicitly test the 13-byte stock response and its padded representation.

The login wire format has no echoed request nonce. An unseen delayed old login reply cannot always be distinguished perfectly from a new one. Treat login success as advisory readiness only: do not publish a route, update a clock or change management state from it. Require the subsequent fresh-tag authenticated PATH response before accepting a primary route. Track last accepted server login timestamp where available and absorb retired responses without reopening work.

Extend the scope binding to dispatch owned login responses delivered inside PATH and, where applicable, ordinary RESPONSE packets. Transient peer data is currently ignored, so that dispatch requires explicit implementation. Intercept only packets owned by the current/retired trace operation; unrelated management traffic retains its existing owner. No reciprocal PATH or local management-route installation should be triggered by trace-owned replies.

A late authenticated discovery reply from an attempt sent in the current transaction may supply a primary candidate while control is still active. Cancel any superseded queued control packet. A control packet already on air remains radio-owned. Later valid replies may add candidates only while another probe can still be selected; they cannot restart completed probing or reporting.

docs.title: 5. Scope policy: make the Zen difference explicit
docs.text:
Separate three values: frozen public reply context, outgoing discovery/login context, and received route-evidence context. A public channel is not a transport region.

Recommended outgoing policy:

  1. Use the sensor's explicitly configured default outbound transport scope.
  2. If none is configured, use a resolved scope from the accepted command.
  3. Otherwise use unscoped flood. Never fan out across guessed regions.

Use the sensor's configured supported discovery hash width (one or two bytes), matching Zen's local-setting approach. Capture it once. Public acknowledgement and final reporting retain the original command's channel/scope/hash-width context. Advert-route TRACE uses the width actually observed for that route.

For current-transaction authenticated discovery, match Zen's response eligibility: accept a valid full-target MAC/decrypted PATH with an actually sent matching tag, valid route and live owner/profile even if its return scope differs. Record that difference; do not silently discard the response. Preserve normal runtime packet validation. Do not copy a returned scope into outgoing or public reply context. This exception is limited to an owned authenticated control response and does not authorize background foreign-scope route harvesting.

Advert fallback eligibility remains conservative: require the observation to match the captured outgoing control scope, or both to be unscoped. Unknown or ambiguous scope observations are retained only as diagnostics, not reusable fallbacks. History and candidates are keyed by full target, stable radio profile, control scope and route width; preserve the request-channel dimension of existing trace outcome history. Advert observations themselves are channel-independent. Temporary radio changes invalidate active history/candidates immediately, even when settings later revert. Persistent hints never restore active validated history automatically.

docs.title: 6. Durable request timestamps and clock diagnostics
docs.text:
Add a sensor-only TraceRequestClock for outgoing login and discovery timestamps. Keep them separate from random TRACE identifiers and wall-clock-dependent cache ages. Use max(current RTC unique value, next durable request value) and reserve an exclusive upper bound before issuing any value from a new block. Proposed reservation: 256 timestamp values.

Persist a version, local full identity, upper bound, sequence and checksum using two independently committed replicated records. A reservation becomes usable only after both replicas durably contain its upper bound. On reboot, take the highest valid bound, start beyond that reserved range, and commit the next range to both replicas before use. This ordering keeps one surviving record sufficient when its partner is torn/corrupt: no value from a newer range may have emitted before both replicas covered it. If neither record is trustworthy, do not issue authenticated timestamps. Missing durability or retry must never reuse a value that could already have reached a peer. If a current RTC jump exceeds the reservation, reserve a new range before transmission. Saturation/overflow is an error.

This is a forward-only request-time floor; do not rewrite the real wall clock from arbitrary peer data. Reserving ahead trades a bounded forward logical-time jump after restart for reduced flash writes. Document that jump and measure write frequency. All new journal/cache I/O is deferred to service-loop work, not RX or TX callbacks. Reserve a timestamp before queueing its packet. The shared allocator covers both trace login and trace discovery, so login cannot consume a timestamp later reused by discovery.

First installation has no record: seed from the local RTC and commit before use, marking clock quality in diagnostics. Migration cannot infer a higher timestamp previously recorded by a remote client from silence. A corrupt existing journal or failed reservation prevents further authenticated requests until safe recovery; use advert fallback where possible. Record the condition precisely instead of claiming the radio or repeater is unreachable. A successful login does not prove that a subsequent sender timestamp exceeds the remote replay floor.

Record RTC source/quality, journal health, request logical time and clock-regression flags. Add a documented local/admin recovery procedure for damaged state or a legacy remote replay floor ahead of trusted time. Never repair by random request tags, resetting the remote ACL, importing Zen's identity or trusting an unmatched login timestamp. Scope this allocator to sensor code; review any other outgoing authenticated operation under the same identity before sharing the mechanism.

docs.title: 7. Verified advert-route collection and construction
docs.text:
Introduce TraceAdvertRouteCache, separate from existing name persistence and validated outcome history. Populate it only from the signature-verified onAdvertRecv callback with the actual received packet. The earlier generic RX observer is not an authenticated advert hook.

Accept the repeater identity from the signed payload, valid flood packet metadata, one/two-byte hash width, compatible resolved scope and stable radio profile. A zero-intermediate flooded advert is a valid direct-target hint. Do not treat a direct/shared contact advert as proof of a zero-hop RF neighbour. Reject malformed paths, unsupported widths and paths requiring more than ten total repeaters, including the target.

If a received target advert has intermediate path [R1, R2, ... Rn] from target towards sensor, infer outward intermediates [Rn, ... R2, R1], append the target's hash, then reverse the outward intermediates for the return leg:

advert: target -> R1 -> R2 -> sensor
TRACE:  sensor -> R2 -> R1 -> target -> R1 -> R2 -> sensor

Build through an explicit advert-to-TraceRoute converter, not the incoming public-command path helper. Test byte order and hop count against actual wire packets for both widths and every supported length.

The advert signature authenticates origin identity/data, not the mutable flood path. Reversing an advert supplies a route hint, not proof of symmetric links or cryptographic proof that a short-hash TRACE passed through that full identity. Existing ambiguous hop labels must remain ambiguous. A new round-trip probe is mandatory; no success, RTT or SNR may be copied from stored observations.

Core first-packet deduplication means duplicate routes from the same advert normally never reach the verified callback. Collect alternatives from different verified advert emissions over time; do not change core deduplication merely to collect duplicate-path copies.

docs.title: 8. Stationary-node cache, persistence and freshness
docs.text:
Recommended limits: 48 full target identities, two distinct advert candidates per identity, with a static route-cache budget of 10 KiB. Store compact intermediate paths (up to nine hashes of two bytes), not duplicate expanded loops. Measure actual struct sizes and enforce bounds. This matches the known-device capacity without relying on mutable name-cache slot indices.

Keep full key, scope, width, stable PHY fingerprint, local observation time, origin advert timestamp/fingerprint, last-hop SNR, provenance and validation/ failure metadata. Stable PHY fingerprint uses actual relevant configuration; a reboot-local generation counter alone cannot identify persisted radio settings. Temporary-radio observations are RAM-only. Clear live candidates/history on any radio change; restored disk hints are candidates requiring new validation.

Use a 24-hour observation-age limit when age can be established reliably. This suits a stationary sensor and infrequent repeater adverts better than a short discovery window. A stored prior TRACE success may rank the route but cannot refresh its advert observation time. Last-hop SNR is a tie-breaker, not an end-to-end score. Prefer previously validated, recent compatible distinct routes; use shorter airtime/hops as further ranking evidence.

Repeated copies of a remembered advert must not refresh observation freshness. Record timestamp/fingerprint regression rather than presenting a replay or a repeater-clock reset as a fresh advertisement. A new clock-regressed observation may be kept as a probationary hint and tested by the bounded user-owned TRACE; it must not become authenticated fresh route evidence. A bounded fingerprint cache cannot prove freshness of every historic signed replay; do not claim it can. No advert receipt itself triggers radio traffic.

Persist a new versioned sidecar file, leaving the existing name-cache schema unchanged. Include local sensor identity, record count/size, stable radio metadata, CRC and observation provenance. Use atomic replacement/backup recovery, a 30-second dirty coalescing delay and at most one routine save per ten minutes. Do not rewrite for unchanged duplicate adverts or per trace request. Save failures retain RAM candidates and last valid disk state; all I/O is outside radio callbacks.

Persisted hints have three eligibility states:

  • Known age, within 24 hours and matching identity/profile/scope: normal fallback.
  • Known expired/incompatible/corrupt: ineligible.
  • Age unknown after reboot without trusted wall time: probationary fallback, tested only by a new bounded probe. Do not reset or invent an advert observation time, or call it freshly discovered. A successful TRACE records new validation time separately. This permits stationary-node recovery without pretending a volatile RTC supplies reliable calendar age.

On repeated route failure, lower rank and prefer another candidate; do not permanently erase a potentially useful stationary route based on one collision. Never return an old selected result without a new probe. Replacing/evicting a name-cache entry cannot retarget a route record: full keys are authoritative.

docs.title: 9. Diagnostics and messages
docs.text:
Add bounded RAM/debug evidence for first-contact stage and route provenance:

  • Full selected identity, attempt/generation, queue/TX/completion timing and packets actually submitted versus started.
  • Guest mode, response protocol validation, returned role and advisory login state.
  • RTC source, durable timestamp/journal health and clock-regression risk.
  • Outgoing scope/width, received scope mode/fingerprint and mismatch accepted.
  • MAC/decryption/tag/owner/profile/scope/path rejection checkpoints where visible.
  • Advert candidate availability, age confidence, width, source and selected route.

Core decryption failures may require a narrow generic observer or target-side packet capture; do not assert visibility that the service does not have. Keep sensor policy out of core Mesh/Dispatcher. Expose safe status/debug summaries, not shared secrets, passwords or raw private keys. Public silence must never be presented as a proven permission denial or replay attack.

Suggested status phases: acknowledging, authenticated discovery, public guest login, discovery after login, waiting for advert route, testing advert route, probe retry and reporting; include remaining overall seconds. Final failures should distinguish no discovered/advert route, no acknowledged guest login, clock/storage issue and attempted-route timeout where evidence supports them. Keep one terminal report; do not emit contradictory preliminary failures while fallback can still succeed. Unknown/ambiguous target errors remain unchanged.

docs.title: 10. Implementation boundaries and sequence
docs.text:
Area Planned responsibility SensorBotService Frozen public/control contexts, fixed deadlines, fallback transitions, one final outcome TraceFirstContact, TraceGuestLogin Bounded initial discovery/login/fresh discovery orchestration and ownership TraceDiscovery Fresh-tag authenticated matching, retired tags and up to two ordinary submissions SensorScopeBinding, Bme680SensorMesh Correct anonymous request creation, owned PATH/RESPONSE dispatch, verified advert packet/context capture TraceRequestClock Atomic timestamp reservation and diagnostics, separate from wall-clock trust TraceAdvertRouteCache and converter Full-key route evidence, compact paths, persistence/aging/ranking Sensor-only configuration hook Public guest/off setting; no upstream NodePrefs or credential reuse RepeaterTraceProbe, timing helpers Shared two-probe count, source-aware candidate selection and remaining-time limits Diagnostics/status and documentation First-contact/scope/clock/provenance visibility and exact bounded behaviour

Implement in reviewable steps: reproduce missing first contact with a production- faithful target; add diagnostic owners and clock journal; implement guest protocol; separate scope contexts; collect/cache advert hints; integrate source selection and global attempt budget; add persistence/reboot recovery; finish regressions, builds and hardware acceptance. Preserve existing working-tree changes and avoid unrelated upstream or Zen modifications.

docs.title: First contact and real 1.18 semantics
docs.text:
• Empty target ACL, public guest enabled: initial discovery silence, one valid anonymous login, fresh-tag discovery/PATH, successful TRACE. No test may pre-register the sensor to make this case pass.
  • Already known client: first ordinary discovery succeeds, no login is sent.
  • Public guest unavailable, protected password, wrong/no login reply, public mode off and unexpected admin grant: bounded transitions to advert fallback; no password guessing or admin operation.
  • Guest success but lost reply, delayed old login, padded/truncated/malformed login, wrong peer/key/MAC/code/role and stale server timestamp: no false route commit. Require fresh ordinary discovery ownership.
  • Remote reboot loses guest state; next operation re-establishes it. Sensor's management ACL/routes remain unchanged; trace-owned PATH causes no reciprocal traffic. Unrelated management traffic keeps its normal owner.

The existing simulated target is insufficient by itself. Add a native harness that executes the production stock 1.18 login/request reply-selection logic or refactor only the needed production policy into shared testable helpers with unchanged behaviour. Retain full encryption/Dispatcher integration. Also test against actual unmodified 1.18 hardware before declaring field success.

docs.title: Advert conversion and login-free fallback
docs.text:
• Verified flooded adverts for one through ten total repeaters and both widths: exact reversed intermediates, appended full-target hash prefix, return loop bytes and normal outward-order/averaged-SNR output.
  • Fresh and restored direct-target zero-intermediate flood hints; direct/shared contact adverts do not create a false direct RF route.
  • Empty remote ACL and unavailable guest access: advert fallback succeeds with no successful login and no seeded remote client entry.
  • No guest credentials, authenticated discovery unavailable and two candidate paths: first broken/asymmetric path fails, second valid route succeeds within the global two-probe and 60-second budgets.
  • Authenticated route first, alternate advert used for the one remaining probe; no third probe or restarted timeout.
  • Invalid advert signature, wrong device type, unsupported width, overlong/ malformed hint and foreign/unresolved scope do not become eligible. Bound looped candidates without mistaking repeated ambiguous short hashes alone for proof of a loop; no route bypasses the round-trip validation requirement.
  • First-packet duplicate handling, later independent adverts, duplicate timestamp/ fingerprint, timestamp regression and replay never manufacture fresh validated outcomes. Last-hop SNR alone cannot establish end-to-end success.
  • A fresh advert during passive wait can supply a route only for the live transaction; cancellation/completion/expiry cannot trigger new traffic.

docs.title: Scope, identity and history
docs.text:
• Same-scope, target-default fallback scope, unscoped fallback and differing reply scope: current full-target/tag authenticated replies follow the explicit acceptance policy; mismatches are recorded, outgoing/public context stays frozen.
  • Wrong MAC/full key/tag/owner/profile rejected even if short hashes match.
  • Same four-character prefix on two identities rejected; same name on different identities cannot mix discovery, persisted hints or history.
  • Both public channels, both configured discovery widths, advert width different from command width, and configured-default versus request-scope selection.
  • Radio change and reversion invalidate active candidates/history; persisted incompatible/temporary hints cannot revive as fresh evidence.

docs.title: Time, persistence and failures
docs.text:
• Sensor reboot with remote replay state retained: reserved timestamps always exceed previously possibly emitted values; login and discovery share allocation.
  • RTC rollback/forward jump, journal first install/migration, wrong local identity, checksum failure, torn replicated-record write, failed reserve, exhaustion and overflow. No uncommitted value may emit; fallback remains possible.
  • Cache save/load, corrupt/truncated/version/count/CRC records, failed save/rename, reboot without trusted UTC, 24-hour boundary, eviction and restored probationary hints. No fabricated observation age or stale result replay.
  • Verify write coalescing/ten-minute route-save limit and timestamp reservation write count. No filesystem or radio estimation in TX callbacks; bounded memory.
  • Every phase at its deadline minus one, exact deadline and plus one; control cutoff 25 seconds, work cutoff 55, final deadline 60, rollover and skipped polls.
  • Packet allocation/queue rejection, CAD/duty contention, definite/uncertain TX failure, missing start/completion and late callbacks after packet reuse.
  • Cancel/status/busy/dedup/rate-limit throughout all new states; a new trace starts after every terminal path without reboot. Never free Dispatcher-owned TX memory.
  • One frozen named acknowledgement, at most one login, two ordinary discoveries, two probes and two terminal report parts. Verify real emitted packet counts, not just state transitions.

docs.title: Regression, firmware and documentation gates
docs.text: Run focused first-contact, advert, clock, scope and lifecycle tests; then all native/native_sensor/native_kiss_modem suites and the working sensor ASan setup. Build sensor, baseline sensor, USB companion, repeater and room-server XIAO nRF52 environments; generate applicable DFU/UF2 artifacts. Run sensor-boundary, whitespace and strict documentation checks. Compare RAM/flash, enforce the route cache budget and validate all generated DFU manifests/CRCs. Record exact revision, results, sizes and SHA256 values in a new validation report. Package an updated uniquely named OTA when requested; do not flash or publish automatically.

docs.title: 12. Hardware acceptance and completion
docs.text:
Capture a working Zen and a sensor transaction against 7188 (stock 1.18) and the additional repeaters Zen can trace without known prior access. Record identities, PHY, packet types/order, scopes, tags and timings without assuming their ACL state.

Required field cases: fresh sensor identity with no remote ACL entry; known client; public guest disabled/protected; successful advert-only fallback; sensor reboot without external RTC; remote reboot; radio change/reversion; one broken advert route and valid alternate; cancellation; and repeated requests after timeout. Preload the stationary sensor with genuine received adverts, reboot it, and verify fallback still works through persisted hints without manufacturing a fresh advert.

Completion requires a successful fresh first-contact case without fixture ACL seeding, a successful login-free advert fallback, preserved result formatting, correct scope/clock diagnostics, all bounded ownership/traffic/timing regressions, and recorded hardware evidence. Software-only validation must be labelled as such until the physical cases are actually performed. No firmware code or tests are changed by this planning document.

docs.title: Approved guest-login timing amendment — 25 October 2026
docs.text: The original eight-second combined guest-login lease is superseded. Use an independent eight-second queue allowance, an airtime-based TX watchdog starting at actual TX start, then an eight-second receive window starting at successful local TX completion. All phases remain bounded by the original 25-second control cutoff, 55-second work cutoff and 60-second overall deadline. Do not extend ordinary discovery stage leases or increase login emissions. An expired queue, failed/missing completion, cancellation, or late/duplicate completion cannot start or reset a receive window. Status distinguishes queued, transmitting and awaiting reply. Tests cover busy-channel queueing, actual completion, exact boundaries, late replies, stale callbacks, cancellation and millisecond wrap.

docs.title: Approved guest-login retry amendment — 25 October 2026
docs.text: Allow two retries of guest login (three transmissions total), with distinct forward-only request timestamps and bounded backoff after an unanswered reply or failed transmission. Stop on accepted login response, unexpected role, cancellation, queue expiry, clock failure or exhausted control time. Retain separate queue, TX and post-completion receive phases. To accommodate three eight-second reply windows plus initial/final discovery, replace the 25-second control cutoff with 40 seconds from acceptance. The 55-second work and 60-second overall cutoffs remain unchanged. This is an upper bound on retries, not a promise all three fit after arbitrary queue delays. The maximum targeted-trace application emissions become ten. Preserve diagnostics slots 0/1/2 and add slots 3/4 for the login retries. Successful-route persistence is not changed.

docs.title: Trace request acknowledgement: implementation and test plan
docs.text:
Status: historical plan; the calculated maximum is superseded by the fixed 60-second cap. Date: 2026-10-25.

See the implementation validation record. The following sections retain the approved implementation and test requirements.

docs.title: Intended behaviour
docs.text:
When the sensor accepts a new trace, immediately schedule this single message:

Trace requested, please wait up to X seconds.

X is the rounded-up maximum duration of the whole accepted operation, including acknowledgement, discovery where needed, both possible probe attempts, settling, retry delay, final grace, and final report delivery. This applies to both !hillvue trace and !hillvue trace 4df5.

Keep the normal sensor-name prefix and send through the accepted request's reply channel and scope. Keep the existing final trace output, sensor-to-selected-repeater ordering, and bidirectional averaged SNR unchanged.

“Immediately” means queued without application jitter after validation and acceptance. Actual transmission must still respect the radio, duty limits, and busy-channel checks. The advertised duration bounds application work and releases trace ownership on the first running service poll at or after its deadline; it cannot guarantee that a receiver hears a packet or that a stalled event loop runs on time. An already transmitting packet remains owned by the Dispatcher until completion or its existing recovery mechanism.

Invalid, ambiguous, unknown-target, rate-limited, duplicate, and busy requests keep their existing responses and do not receive this acknowledgement. Neither trace status nor trace cancel starts another acknowledgement or resets a deadline.

docs.title: Acceptance and lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Parse the request and apply existing deduplication, rate limits, and busy handling.
  2. Validate the route for a bare trace, or resolve a targeted prefix to one full repeater identity. Validate supported path widths and other start prerequisites.
  3. Capture the full target or original route, reply context, radio profile, and monotonic acceptance time. Compute the maximum budget before marking the request accepted. Reject unsupported or unrepresentable timing configurations with a clear error.
  4. Freeze X, the acknowledgement text, and an absolute transaction deadline. Charge the accepted command once under the existing rate policy.
  5. Enter a separate, bounded acknowledgement stage. Attempt transmission with zero application delay. Once the acknowledgement completes, fails, or exhausts its allowance, proceed with tracing regardless of acknowledgement success. Do not wait for a remote receipt acknowledgement.
  6. Start discovery for a targeted trace, or the existing settling/probe flow for a bare trace. Discovery and probe queue timers start after the acknowledgement stage; acknowledgement airtime must not consume their admission budgets.
  7. Run the existing trace attempts and final report within the frozen overall deadline. Finish early whenever possible.
  8. At expiry, stop further trace admissions, cancel only owned queued packets, retire transaction callbacks, and release busy state. Do not begin another report budget after expiry.

Use a small independent acknowledgement owner, proposed as TraceRequestAcknowledgement. It must not reuse the final TraceReportDelivery state or an ordinary reply queue with an unbounded retry lifetime. States should distinguish waiting, queued, transmitting, and terminal outcomes. Permit local retries only while emission is definitely known not to have occurred and within the admission deadline. Once transmission starts or emission is uncertain, do not create another acknowledgement copy.

Cancellation, radio-profile invalidation, or an early terminal outcome must remove any acknowledgement still queued. Late callbacks must be matched to their owning packet/transaction and cannot mutate a newer trace. Preserve Dispatcher ownership of packets already on air.

docs.title: Budget calculation
docs.text:
Add a pure budget composer alongside the existing timing policy. Use 64-bit intermediates and enforce the existing wrap-safe maximum interval of 0x7FFFF000 milliseconds. Never silently clamp a combined budget below the time its phases can consume.

Initial conservative policy:

Symbol Allowance Q Existing discovery/probe queue admission: 10,000 ms each QA New acknowledgement queue admission: 10,000 ms aMax Airtime estimate for MAX_TRANS_UNIT under the captured radio profile W Existing transmitWatchdog(aMax) A Acknowledgement: QA + W D Discovery receive allowance: attemptTimeout(10, aMax) Pmax Probe receive allowance using the maximum supported ten-repeater loop packet, including two-byte hop hashes P0 Bare trace: allowance for its captured original route; targeted trace: Pmax P1 Pmax, since a fresh alternate route may be longer than the first S Existing hard settling cap: 2,500 ms J Maximum retry pause: 2,000 ms G Existing final grace: 3,000 ms R Existing reportBudget(aMax) F Existing failure report allowance: 10,000 ms L Conservative terminal delivery allowance: max(R + 2*W, F + W) M Explicit processing reserve: 1,000 ms

Calculate:

discovery = targeted ? 2 * (Q + D) : 0
total_ms = A + discovery + S + (Q + P0) + J + (Q + P1) + G + L + M
X = ceil(total_ms / 1000)
deadline = accepted_at + total_ms

The acknowledgement's maximum-frame allowance avoids a circular dependency between the number of digits in X and acknowledgement airtime. Cache the actual packet's airtime/watchdog before enqueueing it; verify it fits the planned allowance. Do not estimate airtime or access radio configuration from a TX-start callback.

During implementation, verify the maximum loop packet length against the actual packet serializer and supported hop count. Receive allowances start at actual TX start and already cover transmission time; do not add that airtime again. Verify they cover the corresponding TX watchdog. The existing absolute report budget covers admission retries and the inter-part gap; do not add those twice. L deliberately reserves conservative TX completion allowances for the final report parts.

Use the captured radio profile for every component. Discovery must remain bounded to two attempts and probes to two attempts. Fresh route observations can shorten actual work, but must not increase the promised maximum. A radio-profile change terminates the transaction rather than recalculating a longer deadline.

The reserve is a scheduling allowance, not permission to extend the deadline. Every admission and retry must also obey the remaining overall budget. Define whether a phase can complete with the remaining time before admitting it; otherwise transition to an appropriate terminal outcome while report time remains. Deadline cleanup itself must work even when no report time remains.

docs.title: Code changes
docs.text:
Area Planned change TraceTimingPolicy.h and, if useful, a small transaction-budget header Pure composition, checked arithmetic, rounded seconds, and wrap-safe remaining-time helpers New TraceRequestAcknowledgement.h Bounded state, immutable text/context, packet ownership, and terminal outcomes SensorBotService.h/.cpp Acceptance snapshot, acknowledgement prelude, fixed deadline, callbacks, cancellation, profile-change handling, and busy ownership Discovery/probe/report helpers Only the interfaces needed to constrain work to the transaction deadline; preserve existing phase timing and recovery semantics PublicChannelSensorBot Preserve parser, deduplication, and rate behaviour; change only if acceptance feedback requires it Native test fixtures Realistic packet airtime, controllable clocks, and acknowledgement/failure observations Public bot and development documentation Explain acknowledgement, conservative maximum, early completion, status, and cancellation

Keep acknowledgement memory bounded and avoid per-request heap allocation. Do not add wire protocols, authentication exchanges, persistent storage, or repeater ACL changes. Authenticated discovery continues to use its existing monotonic RTC timestamp, independently of transaction identifiers and millisecond deadlines.

Extend trace status to identify the acknowledgement stage and show remaining overall seconds alongside useful existing phase detail. Keep trace cancel usable throughout acknowledgement, discovery, probing, grace, and final reporting, including when normal start-command rate slots are exhausted.

docs.title: Budget and timer tests
docs.text:
• Independently calculate expected totals for bare and targeted requests. Cover one through ten repeaters, both supported hash widths, short and maximum-sized packets, and representative fast/slow radio profiles.
  • Confirm targeted budgets include two discovery admissions and receive windows. Confirm bare budgets exclude discovery and allow a longer second route.
  • Confirm acknowledgement admission, report splitting, maximum retry delay, settling, grace, and conservative TX completion allowances are included exactly as specified.
  • Test millisecond-to-second rounding, digit boundaries in X, zero or invalid airtime estimates, checked addition, maximum safe intervals, and rejection rather than unsafe saturation.
  • Exercise acceptance near millisecond rollover. Check deadline minus one millisecond, the exact deadline, deadline plus one, and service polls that jump across several phase boundaries.
  • Verify queue, discovery reply, status, and retry events never move the original deadline.

docs.title: Acceptance and acknowledgement tests
docs.text:
• Accepted bare and targeted commands produce the exact message body once, using the expected node prefix, channel, and scope.
  • Invalid syntax, missing bare routes, unknown/ambiguous target prefixes, busy responses, duplicates, rate limits, status, and cancellation produce no request acknowledgement.
  • No added application jitter; ordinary Dispatcher channel access rules still apply.
  • The acknowledgement does not overwrite final report text, target identity, route state, SNR values, or reply context and does not consume another command-rate slot.
  • Discovery/probe admission clocks begin after the acknowledgement stage, including when the acknowledgement occupies the radio for longer than a probe's normal queue allowance.
  • Allocation failures, queue rejection, definitely-not-sent failures, uncertain emission, missing TX-start, and missing completion all leave the acknowledgement stage within its bound. No uncertain or started transmission creates another emitting copy.
  • Oversized prefixed messages and formatting failures have a defined bounded outcome; tracing does not stay busy because acknowledgement formatting failed.

docs.title: Lifecycle and recovery tests
docs.text:
• Cancel at each acknowledgement state and every subsequent phase; confirm owned queued packets are removed and a new trace can start.
  • Change the radio profile during each acknowledgement state and later phases; no recalculated deadline or stale acknowledgement survives.
  • Deliver delayed discovery replies, TX-start callbacks, and TX-complete/failure callbacks after cancellation, expiry, completion, and a subsequent accepted request. They must not change the newer transaction.
  • Hold the channel busy or deny transmission until admission expiry. Exercise both discovery failures, first-probe timeout, retry, final grace, and two-part final delivery.
  • Cross the overall deadline with queued and in-flight packets. Queued packets are cancelled; Dispatcher-owned transmitting packets are not freed or reused by the service. Busy state and stale-callback protection remain correct.
  • Ensure expiry never opens another full failure-report window or produces a contradictory failure after a possibly emitted success report.
  • Preserve trace RTT measurement from actual probe TX start, averaged link SNR, alternate-route selection, history scoping, late-result fallback, and existing final formatting.

docs.title: Real Dispatcher and network tests
docs.text:
Use the real Dispatcher and existing sensor network fixtures, beyond state-only mocks, to verify packet-pool ownership, actual TX-start timing, CAD/duty delays, cancellation of queued packets, failed transmission ownership, and callback order. Model realistic slow airtimes so an unrealistically short test TX duration cannot hide contention between acknowledgement and tracing.

Cover both public channels, scoped and unscoped replies, direct and multi-hop paths, and final reports of one and two parts. Assert bounded packet counts and balanced packet-pool ownership after completion and recovery. Keep regressions behavioural rather than duplicating implementation formulas in the test oracle.

docs.title: Build and regression gates
docs.text:
Run these after implementation, with results recorded against the implemented revision:

  1. Focused acknowledgement/budget tests plus existing public-bot, target-trace, trace-reliability, network, and Dispatcher tests.
  2. Full native suites: pio test -e native -e native_sensor -e native_kiss_modem.
  3. Sensor AddressSanitizer suite using the documented working host configuration; distinguish infrastructure failures from test failures.
  4. Firmware builds and applicable DFU/UF2 generation for Xiao_nrf52_bme680_sensor, Xiao_nrf52_sensor_baseline, Xiao_nrf52_companion_radio_usb, Xiao_nrf52_repeater, and Xiao_nrf52_room_server.
  5. bash bin/check-sensor-boundaries.sh, whitespace checks, and the strict documentation build.
  6. Compare sensor RAM/flash with the pre-change build; confirm bounded memory use and no unintended cross-role dependency.

Use the installed PlatformIO executable or its virtual environment where needed. Preserve existing unrelated working-tree changes. Do not publish or install firmware as part of planning. Produce a fresh OTA package only after implementation/build validation if requested, with revision and checksum recorded.

docs.title: Physical radio acceptance
docs.text:
On test hardware, record firmware revision, radio settings, channel/scope, topology, and observed timings. Test bare and targeted traces, a known target such as 4df5, fast and slow profiles, reachable and silent targets, and a busy channel. Capture acceptance, acknowledgement TX, each probe TX, terminal reply, and busy release times.

Check that the acknowledgement has no added application delay, its X matches the calculated frozen maximum, and normal success completes early. Repeat the original scenario: start trace 4df5, request another trace after 30 seconds, inspect status, then cancel or wait for the advertised deadline. A busy reply before that deadline can be correct; a busy transaction persisting beyond expiry on a running service loop is a failure. Confirm a subsequent trace starts after terminal cleanup.

Verify cancellation during acknowledgement and discovery, a lost final reply, and recovery after channel contention. Physical receipt and SNR accuracy require this hardware evidence; native tests alone do not establish them.

docs.title: Implementation order and completion criteria
docs.text:
1. Add checked budget composition and independent timing tests.
  2. Add the bounded acknowledgement owner and ownership/failure tests.
  3. Integrate acceptance, acknowledgement prelude, fixed deadline, status, cancellation, and profile-change cleanup.
  4. Add real Dispatcher/network regressions, including late callbacks and slow-radio contention.
  5. Update user/developer documentation, run all regression/build gates, and record hardware results separately.

Complete when every accepted start schedules at most one emitting acknowledgement, the displayed maximum covers every permitted phase, all exits release trace ownership within the defined software deadline contract, and existing trace output and recovery behaviour pass regression tests. Mark hardware validation pending until actually performed. This document itself changes no firmware.

docs.title: Sensor trace scope and Dispatcher regression plan
docs.text: Status: implemented; see validation and physical acceptance status. Date: 24 October 2026.

docs.title: Objective and evidence
docs.text:
Preserve the scope of bot replies through delayed delivery, isolate trace route evidence by scope, and add focused Dispatcher lifecycle tests. Keep the existing bounded two-attempt trace algorithm, RTT definition, radio ownership, report deadlines, channel behaviour and rate limits.

Review found that Bme680SensorMesh::sendFlood() calls plain Mesh::sendFlood(), bypassing upstream request/default reply-scope selection. History currently distinguishes route, channel and radio profile, but not transport scope. Candidate matching uses the accepted command ciphertext without scope discrimination. These are implementation gaps; their RF consequences have not been demonstrated on hardware.

The review ran 76 passing cases across test_sensor_integration, test_sensor_storage, test_sensor_routes and test_sensor_trace_reliability. This is a baseline, not the complete release validation suite.

Authenticated discovery is absent from the sensor trace flow. Do not introduce discovery, RTC replay-protection changes, telemetry-permission diagnostics or requester identity as part of this work. Traces follow observed repeater hashes and return to the sensor. Full identities cannot be inferred from those hashes. Ambiguous cached names already fall back to hex and have regression coverage.

docs.title: 1. Establish regression coverage first
docs.text:
Add test/test_sensor_dispatcher/test_sensor_dispatcher.cpp, adapted from the five focused tests on local zen/main:test/test_trace_dispatcher/. Use real Dispatcher and StaticPoolPacketManager with controllable radio/clock fixtures, under native_sensor and its sanitizer environment. Avoid adding Dispatcher sources to the unrelated native environment just for these tests.

Required assertions:

  • Scheduled delay produces no TX-start callback until the radio accepts a send; callback time equals the actual start, not enqueue time.
  • A busy receiver/channel defers sending without starting the RTT clock.
  • A rejected radio start calls failure once, never calls TX-start, and returns exactly one allocation to the pool. A later allocation remains usable.
  • Cancelling one queued packet leaves another queued packet untouched; repeated cancellation is harmless. An in-flight packet cannot be cancelled through the queued-packet API and remains owned by Dispatcher until completion/watchdog.
  • A normal consumer with no TX-start override retains its baseline lifecycle.

Keep existing service integration tests for queue expiry, pool reuse, late fallback and committed failure. Add service-level busy-channel coverage so that the Dispatcher callback and probe RTT are tested together, rather than relying only on separate unit tests.

Acceptance: these tests pass before scope changes; any pre-existing failure is triaged separately instead of silently changing core timing behaviour.

docs.title: 2. Introduce a value-owned reply context
docs.text:
Add a small application reply-context value, carried explicitly through SensorBotTransport, SensorBotService, PublicResponseQueue and TraceReportDelivery. It contains the channel, selected reply scope key (or explicit unscoped state), and reply path-hash width. Keep request scope identity separate from the selected reply scope: an unresolved request may use the default for its reply without proving that its observed path belongs to that default.

Capture context synchronously when an accepted command is handled. Store values, not Packet/RegionEntry pointers, mutable globals, region names, or packet-specific 16-bit transport codes. Transport codes must be recalculated for each newly encrypted reply packet using its captured key. Do not persist or log keys.

The selected reply scope follows existing chooseReplyScope() semantics:

Accepted request Reply selection Resolved transport scope A A, even if default is B Explicit unscoped flood Unscoped, even if a default exists Unresolved transport scope Current usable default, otherwise unscoped Direct request, if supported by a bot command Current usable default, otherwise unscoped

Snapshot the selection at acceptance. A later default-region change or unrelated received packet must not redirect already pending replies. A new command uses the new configuration. Radio configuration cancellation/deadline behaviour stays as currently implemented; scope changes do not restart report budgets.

The necessary region map and scope fields are private in SensorMesh. Add a minimal generic protected API to capture a value-owned reply scope and emit a packet with an explicit captured scope. Reuse existing resolution and sendFloodScoped() logic. Keep bot-specific types and policy out of upstream sensor and core code; do not expose mutable region-map internals. Prefer a shared generic scope-selection helper used by both the existing synchronous sendFloodReply() and the new capture API, preserving current behaviour.

Acceptance: baseline consumers retain identical scope selection and wire format. Application code can capture and send without holding receive-context pointers. The boundary script continues to reject bot-policy leakage.

docs.title: 3. Propagate context through every reply path
docs.text:
Update the service and queue APIs so context is required at scheduling time, including single-part replies, ordinary multipart replies, rescheduling after allocation failure, trace success, timeout/error reports and late fallback.

Keep an immutable active-trace context independent of the new request's context. A busy notice uses the new request context; the active trace's eventual result uses the original context. Before closing/resetting a trace, preserve the context needed to construct its final report. Each queued multipart entry owns its own context. Trace probes remain direct MeshCore TRACE packets; do not add flood scope fields to direct trace frames.

Regression matrix:

  • Scope A request/default B replies in A; unscoped request/default B remains unscoped; unresolved scope uses B or unscoped when no default exists.
  • Interleave A and B on both Public and #hillvue, including multipart replies. Assert every emitted part has the original channel, selected scope and width.
  • While trace A runs, receive request B and a busy notice. Verify A's success, retry failure and late fallback remain in A, while the notice uses B.
  • Change the default and process unrelated receive traffic before delayed send, allocation retry and second-part send. Context remains unchanged.
  • Decrypt each reply and independently verify its transport code using the expected key. Ensure multipart packets get their own calculated codes.
  • Repeat cancellation, expiry, uncertain TX failure and pool-exhaustion tests; check bounded traffic and complete pool recovery after terminal work drains.

docs.title: 4. Isolate request candidates and route history by scope
docs.text:
Introduce an explicit request-scope identity: unscoped, resolved key, or unresolved. For resolved history compare the complete key bytes, or an adequately sized full-key fingerprint; do not use a region ID/name or 16-bit transport code as a durable identity. Keep existing channel, radio profile, exact route and TTL checks. Full-key changes naturally separate records without changing the fixed four-entry bound.

For unresolved transport scopes, do not read/write cross-transaction history. Within a transaction, accept alternate copies only with the same ciphertext, transport route class and conservative matching transport-code tuple. This may discard valid alternatives but avoids asserting a scope identity that cannot be resolved. Document residual short-code ambiguity. Resolved alternatives must resolve to the original key; unscoped and scoped copies never mix.

Candidate observation occurs through logRx, before normal receive dispatch. Resolve scope from the observed packet itself using a side-effect-free adapter operation. Never use recv_pkt_region left by the previous packet. Keep this operation bounded and avoid persistent writes. Do not change ciphertext-match, path validation, three-candidate capacity or settling hard limits.

Required tests:

  • Identical routes/channel/radio in scopes A and B have independent outcomes.
  • Unscoped, resolved and unresolved requests cannot borrow each other's history.
  • Same scope key with a renamed region retains identity; changed key under the same region ID does not reuse evidence.
  • Different-scope copies of identical ciphertext do not enter candidates or extend quiet time. Same-scope copies still qualify.
  • History cannot supply a candidate not observed for the current command.
  • TTL, capacity eviction, radio changes, temporary apply/revert and millis wrap retain their existing behaviour.
  • Completion/cancellation clears candidate state. Late old results or command copies cannot update history, queue probes or alter a newer transaction.
  • Preserve intentional late-result acceptance while a transaction remains open, including replacement of an unsent failure and original-attempt fallback.

Acceptance: only fresh observations in the current request scope can be retried; history changes ranking only and never supplies freshness or full-node identity.

docs.title: 5. Test the production binding, not only the service mock
docs.text:
Extend the native fixtures with real transport-code generation and region/key resolution. Add tests for the generic SensorMesh scope-capture API or a shared production helper that it directly uses, plus a thin-adapter test proving the Bme680 binding calls that path. Resolve embedded build dependencies with small existing-style board/storage stubs if necessary. A mock returning a chosen scope alone is insufficient evidence for the integration gap being fixed.

Add deterministic network cases in test_sensor_network: a relay rejecting unscoped floods must forward a correctly scoped report; a wrong-scope report must fail the same check. Cover both channels, delayed multipart and retry failure. The filter must validate transport codes rather than a fixture label. Keep the model explicitly separate from RF acceptance.

docs.title: 6. Validation and documentation
docs.text:
Run focused tests after each change, then the complete release checks once the implementation is stable. Use the installed pio executable; on the reviewed machine it is /home/matt/.platformio/penv/bin/pio.

pio test -e native -e native_sensor -e native_kiss_modem
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 pio test -e native_sensor_asan
bash bin/check-sensor-boundaries.sh
pio run -e Xiao_nrf52_bme680_sensor
pio run -e Xiao_nrf52_bme680_sensor -t create_uf2
pio run -e Xiao_nrf52_sensor_baseline
mkdocs build --strict

Also run the remaining firmware targets required by .github/workflows/sensor-firmware.yml, particularly consumers affected by any generic SensorMesh header/API change. Ensure the new tests are selected by CI and the sanitizer environment; adjust source filters only when required.

Update the public-bot and development documentation with scope-selection rules, snapshot behaviour, unresolved-scope limitations and new automated coverage. Preserve conservative failure wording and ambiguity fallback. Record test counts, compiler warnings, firmware flash/static RAM deltas against the same revision/toolchain baseline, and UF2/DFU artifact paths and checksums. Confirm no key material or bot policy leaks into logs/core code. Do not copy old resource figures as new measurements.

docs.title: 7. Physical acceptance gate
docs.text:
Use a controlled sensor/companion/two- or three-repeater setup. Record firmware revision, radio settings, scope keys by non-secret labels, topology, hash width and repeat counts. Capture timestamps and decoded packets with temporary test instrumentation; avoid logging key material.

  1. Set repeaters to reject unscoped flooding and confirm scoped command and final report delivery. Verify unscoped and wrong-scope negative controls.
  2. Repeat on Public and #hillvue, one- and two-byte path hashes, including a long multipart report and interleaved requests from different scopes.
  3. Change the default scope while a report is pending. The old report keeps its accepted context; the next command uses the new selection rules.
  4. Exercise contention and slower radio settings. Measure enqueue and actual TX-start separately; RTT excludes local waiting and follows the existing airtime-aware timeout policy.
  5. Exercise retry success, late first-attempt fallback and a lost result. Confirm at most two probe submissions and no contradictory final reports.
  6. Correlate distinct receive SNRs at each outward hop with report order using repeater logs or controlled link differences. Do not infer correctness from simulation alone.
  7. Check post-test telemetry, admin access, node identity, one-minute sampling and normal channel commands. Smoke-test UF2 flashing and DFU update.

Record physical checks as passed, failed or not run. Automated completion does not imply physical acceptance.

docs.title: Delivery sequence and completion criteria
docs.text:
Use reviewable commits: (1) Dispatcher tests; (2) generic scope capture and its baseline tests; (3) bot context propagation; (4) candidate/history isolation; (5) production-binding/network coverage and documentation. Put each feature's regressions in the same commit as its implementation where practical.

Software completion requires all relevant CI suites, sanitizer checks, boundary checks, firmware builds and documentation validation to pass; bounded memory and packet ownership must remain intact. Record physical acceptance separately and leave deployment/installation as a subsequent action. If regression tests expose an unrelated defect, document it and address it separately unless it blocks this scope fix.

docs.title: Destination trace implementation and validation
docs.text: Date: 25 October 2026 (Australia/Sydney). Working tree based on 99dc1448, extending the average SNR implementation.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
!hillvue trace 4df5 resolves exactly four case-insensitive hexadecimal characters against full public keys in the verified, named repeater-advert cache. One match selects that identity; no match or multiple matches produce an unknown/ambiguous repeater error without transmitting discovery. Invalid syntax is ignored like other invalid bot commands. Bare trace is preserved.

The sensor originates a standard authenticated flooded base-telemetry request. It discovers a fresh outbound path, appends the selected target and reverses the intermediate path to construct the loop back to itself. Direct neighbours and one through ten repeaters including the target are supported, with one- or two-byte path hashes. Unsupported request widths fail before discovery; unsupported/oversized returned paths are never probed.

The public report remains Trace: <elapsed> ms RTT (avg SNR), with each node listed once from sensor to target, paired directional averages, and no separate return-node list. RTT begins at actual loop TX start; discovery, settling and queue time are excluded. Retry and original-route fallback reuse the existing probe and immutable report-delivery policies.

The target must already recognise/permit the sensor identity. The bot does not log in, add ACL entries or grant permissions. Missing responses report discovery timeout, not that the target is unreachable. Unknown remote identity, permissions, clock replay checks, congestion and RF conditions may all prevent discovery.

docs.title: State and ownership
docs.text:
• One transaction remains busy through discovery, tracing and bounded reporting. There are at most two discovery submissions and two trace submissions. Discovery admission is bounded to ten seconds per attempt, with the existing 250/500/1000 ms backoff and bounded jitter. Its receive timeout uses the ten-repeater airtime allowance, starting at TX start (at least 30 seconds).
  • Discovery tags come from getCurrentTimeUnique(), independently of random trace identifiers. Authenticated PATH data must match the selected full key, a transmitted discovery tag and the captured discovery scope.
  • Radio profile changes cancel queued targeted work before Dispatcher can start it. In-flight ownership remains with Dispatcher. A late first discovery can cancel an unsent discovery retry. Matching late PATHs cannot restart a closed transaction or create reciprocal traffic.
  • The production scope/peer adapter is instantiated by native tests too. It adds at most three transient full-key peer contexts to the baseline bounded ACL search: current transaction and two retired contexts, all RAM-only. It does not change the sensor ACL or management route arrays.
  • The sensor has no other outbound RESPONSE/PATH request owner. Its custom binding consumes unowned RESPONSE/PATH messages rather than installing them as management routes, including responses older than the transient peer ring. Normal non-response management PATH and authenticated request callbacks keep their existing runtime owner. This policy is confined to the custom adapter.
  • The generic Mesh PATH decoder now checks that the encoded path plus its extra-type byte fits inside the authenticated decrypted payload before reading either extra fields or invoking a callback. A valid encoding with truncated content is rejected; no bot policy was added to core.
  • Reports/discovery keep their original channel, scope key and hash width. Intervening traffic or default-scope changes do not redirect the transaction. Candidate routes must come from fresh authenticated responses; recent four-entry history ranks them but cannot invent a route. Targeted history includes the full target key, full scope key, channel and radio profile, and cannot borrow bare-trace evidence. History expires after fifteen minutes.

Short routing hashes remain hints rather than proof of per-hop identity. Cached ambiguity still displays a hash rather than a confident repeater name.

docs.title: Fixed 60-second trace cap
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-25. Applies to the current working tree on meshcore/sensor, based on 69891ef8 plus the existing recovery and acknowledgement changes. This supersedes the calculated multi-minute timeout in the earlier acknowledgement record.

docs.title: Behaviour and implementation
docs.text:
Both !hillvue trace and !hillvue trace 7188 acknowledge an accepted start with:

BME680 Sensor: Trace requested, please wait up to 60 seconds.

The monotonic deadline is frozen at acceptance. TraceTransactionBudget now provides a fixed 60,000 ms duration and a 5,000 ms reporting reserve rather than summing maximum ten-hop phase allowances. The limit covers acknowledgement, discovery, queue waits, settling, probes, retries, grace and final reporting. Duplicate/start-busy/status requests and new routes cannot extend it.

At actual TX start, existing airtime/hop receive allowances are shortened to share the remaining work time:

Attempt Maximum share of remaining time before the 55-second cutoff Discovery 1 One quarter Discovery 2 One third Probe 1 One half Probe 2 All remaining work time

The first discovery leaves room for a discovery retry and two probes. A quick successful discovery leaves more time for probing. Shorter existing phase allowances remain shorter. Queue delays are included because the share is calculated at actual TX start, using only timer arithmetic; observers do not query the transmitting radio. A retry is not admitted if its estimated TX watchdog plus requested delay cannot fit before the work cutoff.

On the first running poll at 55 seconds, unfinished work ends. A previously stored valid fallback result can still be reported; otherwise the sensor queues Trace: discovery timed out or Trace: no result before timeout, according to the stage. A timeout generated at this cutoff has no application jitter. Its report budget is limited to the original deadline. A report already active is preserved and never replaced by a conflicting failure.

At 60 seconds, owned queued packets are cancelled and the transaction releases its trace slot. Packets already on air remain exclusively under Dispatcher ownership until completion/watchdog recovery. Late results, discovery replies and callbacks do not reopen the expired transaction. Success can finish much earlier, and the existing node order, averaged SNR and final result format are preserved. Status includes the current phase and overall time remaining.

The cap bounds application work on a running service loop, not successful RF receipt. Slow/congested links can time out despite being reachable. An in-flight frame cannot be recalled, and a blocked application cannot clean up until its next poll. Final multipart delivery is best effort within the same deadline; remaining unsent parts cannot continue past 60 seconds.

  • Work and transaction boundaries at 55 and 60 seconds, adjacent milliseconds, rollover and delayed polls.

docs.text:
No device has been flashed and no hardware acceptance has been performed. Check a successful and a silent target, bare and targeted commands, busy/slow radio, cancellation, 55/60-second cleanup and a subsequent request without reboot.

This change does not fix or establish the cause of the sensor discovery failure for 7188. Zen succeeding from the same location does not establish sensor identity/ACL eligibility, scope equivalence or acceptance of returning replies. That read-only comparison and packet-level diagnosis remain a separate investigation. The 60-second limit shortens waiting and guarantees bounded software ownership; it does not claim that the destination is unreachable.

docs.title: Average bidirectional trace SNR validation
docs.text: Date: 24 October 2026 (Australia/Sydney). Working tree based on 99dc1448, following the scope implementation.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
Each outward repeater is listed once, in order from the sensor towards the requester. Its value averages the readings for both directions of its link to its preceding node. The first link uses the sensor's final receive reading as its return sample. The requester link is not traversed by the trace.

For N repeaters and zero-based outward index i, the pair is raw sample i and raw sample 2*N - 1 - i. Both quarter-dB bytes are converted to signed integers before summing; division by eight produces dB without truncating the possible eighth-dB average. Formatting rounds once, to one decimal place.

The header now reads Trace: <elapsed> ms RTT (avg SNR). Raw directional samples remain intact in diagnostics. Retry success uses its own route and samples; late first-attempt fallback uses the original route and both original readings. RTT, packet format, scope, channel, timeout, retry and bounded multipart delivery policies are unchanged. Existing report size/truncation limits still apply; the label does not add any radio probes.

Example checked through real forwarding, for both hash widths:

Listed repeater Outward SNR Return SNR Displayed SNR First from sensor -6 dB -2 dB -4.0 dB Second +2 dB 0 dB +1.0 dB Third -10 dB +2 dB -4.0 dB

This is the arithmetic mean of two reported dB values, not a time average or weakest-direction score. It can conceal directional asymmetry.

The packet-medium suite adds one case covering actual outward and return forwarding with independently configured directional SNRs, both hash widths and exclusion of the requester link. Existing scope/multipart and ten-repeater report tests continue to pass.

docs.title: Named destination trace acknowledgement validation
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-25. Current working tree on meshcore/sensor, based on adc6cab4 (trace), which includes the existing recovery, acknowledgement and fixed 60-second cap changes. No commit, flash or physical radio acceptance is implied.

docs.title: Implemented behaviour
docs.text:
A uniquely known 7188 named Hilltop Repeater produces:

BME680 Sensor: Trace requested to Hilltop Repeater, please wait up to 60 seconds.

The same cache lookup returns the full identity and copied destination label. Full display words and case are preserved; the separate compact hop formatter still removes Repeater as before. ASCII controls/whitespace are normalized, valid UTF-8 is preserved, and a known identity with no usable name uses lowercase 7188. Unknown and ambiguous prefixes retain their errors and clear lookup outputs. Adverts without a name field retain existing cache admission behaviour. No cache schema, authentication or ACL changes were made.

The acknowledgement formatter snapshots sensor prefix and destination before queueing. A rename or cache eviction cannot change queued/retried text or the full key used for discovery. It fits one 160-byte public message, truncating only the destination at a valid UTF-8 boundary when necessary. If no meaningful label fits, the prefix fallback is tried; if that cannot fit either, formatting fails before acceptance. Fixed text and the timeout suffix cannot be truncated.

Bare acknowledgement, final trace formatting, node ordering, averaged SNR, channels/scopes, command controls and the 55/60-second cutoffs are preserved. The earlier sensor-versus-Zen discovery failure remains a separate investigation.

docs.title: Test evidence
docs.text:
New tests cover:

  • Full display name with Repeater, normalized whitespace/control characters, unnamed/invalid UTF-8 fallback, maximum stored UTF-8 names and cache replacement.
  • Clearing full-key and label outputs on unknown or ambiguous resolution; unchanged compact hop labels and existing cache persistence behaviour.
  • Exact 160-byte acknowledgement, one-byte overflow, UTF-8-safe truncation, fallback when no valid destination character fits, and impossible prefixes.
  • Frozen mutable input across definitely-unsent and uncertain failures.
  • Real Dispatcher named acknowledgement before discovery, uppercase prefix, same-name/different-key identities, and decryption with the selected full key. Decryption with the other identity fails, ensuring names do not select keys.
  • Queue rejection followed by cache/sensor rename, and eviction of the selected cache entry before retry; emitted text and discovery identity remain frozen.
  • Scoped real-network delivery with exact named acknowledgement on both channels and both path-hash widths, alongside unchanged final results.

Existing acknowledgement ownership/recovery, unknown/ambiguous rejection, rate-limit/control, timing, fallback, SNR, scope and packet-pool regressions also run. Legacy exact-phase tests explicitly isolate acknowledgement through their transport seam; dedicated acknowledgement tests and network tests use the real Dispatcher. The seam's message recognition now includes both acknowledgement forms.
